searchalertapi.description: Read-only search of saved alerts in the alert center for investigation, locating incidents by filters, and inspecting parent/child relationships. The MCP tool name is alert.search; pass the filter object directly as arguments. ALERT_BASE permission is required; availability of this tool and the discovery APIs below depends on server MCP configuration. Elasticsearch finds IDs, then records are read from the database. An empty tbodyList means no records were returned by this search, not that raw ingestion records are empty; use /alert/origin/search for ingestion records and /alert/get for an alert detail. Ordinary filters and the advanced rule are combined with AND. Within statusList/sourceList/levelList, values are OR; within markNameList/teamIdList, values are AND. Default tree returns only top-level alerts; explicitly use searchMode=flat to search both parents and children. Without a closure-state filter, both open and closed alerts are searched; for open alerts use const_isClose equal ["0"] in rule. Use real identifiers rather than display labels or invented status/severity values. Read business fields from tbodyList; theadList is display metadata. Read pages sequentially and stop when tbodyList is empty. The top-level wordList is an array of keyword token strings, may be null without a keyword, and is for display only.

children.description: Replace 10001 with a real parent id from an earlier search. Returns direct children only, excluding the parent.
children.title: Search direct children of a parent

open.description: Search all levels, combining open state and a tokenized title match for CPU with AND. isClose=0 means open and is separate from configurable status identifiers; no status/severity enumeration is assumed.
open.title: Search open CPU alerts with an advanced rule

recent.description: Search all levels for alerts updated within the last 24 hours matching CPU via full-text search, newest first. Replace CPU with the actual search term.
recent.title: Search recently updated CPU alerts

roots.description: Search the first page of top-level alerts with no closure-state restriction. Records can contain childAlertCount.
roots.title: Search top-level alerts

attrfilterlist.help: Object array: {"name":"attr_actualAttributeName","valueList":["value1","value2"]}. Entries are AND; values within an entry are OR using indexed exact values. Discover searchable name values via /alert/attr/list with {"kind":"attr","isSearch":1}. Entries with empty valueList are ignored. Do not filter unindexed attributes.

currentpage.help: One-based page number, default 1 when omitted. Increment by 1 for the next page while preserving all other filters. Always use a positive integer.

fromalertid.help: Only effective in tree mode. Use an existing alert ID to search its direct children, excluding the parent itself and deeper descendants. Omit to search top-level alerts. Ignored in flat mode.

keyword.help: Tokenized full-text search across alert index fields, not a title substring match. Multiple query terms use AND. A numeric keyword also adds an exact alert-ID filter; use rule for searching numeric text in a specific field.

level.help: This field is not used as a filter by the current search implementation. Use levelList, including for a single severity.

levellist.help: Integer array matching any severity (OR). Obtain real values from level in /alert/level/list, not label/name. Do not infer severity from numeric magnitude.

marknamelist.help: String array; alerts must have all specified tags (AND). Use tag name, not uuid. Omitted or empty arrays do not filter tags.

pagesize.help: Default 20. Positive integers are capped at 1000; nonpositive values retain the default. Prefer 20–100 to limit response size.

rule.help: Shape: {"conditionGroupList":[{"conditionList":[{"id":"const_title","expression":"like","valueList":["CPU"]}],"conditionRelList":[]}],"conditionGroupRelList":[]}. Use name from /alert/attr/list with {"isSearch":1} as id and choose expression from that attribute's expressionList; valueList must be an array. const_ addresses built-in fields; attr_ addresses attrObj fields. conditionRelList joins adjacent conditions in a group; conditionGroupRelList joins adjacent groups. Both use and/or with exactly entry-count minus 1 values; use [] for one entry. AND precedes OR within groups and between groups. Missing or mismatched relation lists fall back to AND. Implemented operators: equal/notequal/like/notlike/gt/lt/gte/lte/range/is-null/is-not-null; use only operators in this implemented list that are also allowed by the attribute. Metadata may include inworktime/outworktime, which this search implementation does not support; do not pass them. equal requires all values as phrase matches; notequal excludes any value; like matches any tokenized value condition; notlike excludes any match. Comparisons use only the first value. range requires exactly two values and is inclusive. Null checks do not need values. Date ranges accept yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss, yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, or Unix milliseconds. A nonempty rule overrides the view rule and is ANDed with ordinary filters; {} does not clear the view rule.

searchmode.help: tree (default): omit fromAlertId for top-level alerts, or supply a parent ID for its direct children. flat: searches all levels and ignores fromAlertId; childAlertCount=0 in this mode does not prove an alert has no children. Both modes return a page list in tbodyList, not an automatically nested tree.

sortdata.help: Example: {"const_updateTime":"desc"}; use asc/desc. Only const_ built-in fields are processed; attr_ sorting is unsupported. Use name for attributes with isSort=true from /alert/attr/list with {"isColumn":1}. Omitted or {} defaults to updateTime descending. Multi-field priority depends on object-key iteration order; prefer one field.

source.help: This field is not used as a filter by the current search implementation. Use sourceList, including for a single source.

sourcelist.help: String array matching any source (OR). Read name from tbodyList of /alert/source/search, not label. Omitted or empty arrays do not filter source.

status.help: This field is not used as a filter by the current search implementation. Use statusList, including for a single status.

statuslist.help: String array matching any status (OR). Obtain identifiers from name in /alert/status/list; label is display text. Omitted or empty arrays do not filter status.

teamidlist.help: String array of team UUIDs, not numeric IDs or team names. Alerts must belong to every specified team (AND). The team#UUID form is accepted and the prefix is stripped.

updatetimehour.help: A positive integer N filters updateTime >= now minus N hours, inclusive. This uses update time, not initial alert time. Omitted or nonpositive values do not add this filter.

viewname.help: Use name from /alert/view/list, not id or label. A nonexistent view causes an error. A nonempty rule overrides the view rule; omitted rule or {} uses the view rule. Ordinary filters still apply. The view also controls theadList; without a view, all-alert column configuration is used.

currentpage.help: Page number returned for this call; populated from index pagination when there are hits.

pagecount.help: Total index pages when there are hits. When this page has no hits, the current implementation retains default 0; this does not prove earlier pages were empty.

pagesize.help: Effective page size, which may differ from tbodyList length.

rownum.help: Total index matches when there are hits; an empty page retains default 0. tree counts the current level; flat counts all levels.

tbodylist.help: Alert objects; [] means no records were returned for this page. Common fields: id, title, level/levelLabel, status/statusName, source/sourceName, isClose (0 open, 1 closed), alertTime/updateTime/closeTime and their Str text forms, fromAlertId, childAlertCount, attrObj, userList, teamList, markList, actionList. Business fields have no const_/attr_ prefix; read custom values from attrObj[actualAttributeName]. Unset fields may be omitted or null; do not assume every field has a value. Child counts are not queried in flat mode. Use /alert/get with id for details.

theadlist.help: Objects typically containing key/title/sort; custom-attribute columns can also contain attrList. const_/attr_ are display column keys, not same-named tbodyList fields. Generated from view/all-alert configuration, not a filter specification.

integration.description: Call an integration during the circuit breaker lifecycle to send circuit-open, aggregated, or recovery information.
integration.label: Call Integration

sendmail.description: Send email during the circuit breaker lifecycle for circuit-open, aggregated, and recovery notifications.
sendmail.label: Send Email

consecutivefailure.description: Track consecutive failures by plugin instance or plugin type and open the circuit when the threshold is reached.
consecutivefailure.label: Consecutive Failure Circuit Breaker

countwindow.description: Track event plugin executions by configured dimensions within a time window and open the circuit when the threshold is exceeded.
countwindow.label: Execution Count Window Circuit Breaker

mailreceiverwindow.description: Track sends by actual email recipient list, then delay and aggregate delivery when the threshold is exceeded.
mailreceiverwindow.label: Email Recipient Circuit Breaker

event.actionhandlerdesc: Add custom operations to the alarm.
event.applyhandlerdesc: Assign the alarm to handlers or teams. Handlers and users in assigned teams can update the alarm status, close the alarm, or delete the alarm.
event.cancelintervalhandlerdesc: Cancel scheduled jobs created by scheduled dispatch plugins in the current alarm type.
event.closehandlerdesc: Closed alarms cannot be modified, and new alarms will no longer be mounted under closed alarms.
event.conditionhandlerdesc: Trigger other event plugins conditionally through configured condition groups, such as sending notifications or assigning handlers.
event.deletehandlerdesc: Physically delete alarm information. Deleted alarms cannot be restored. Use with caution.
event.emailhandlerdesc: Send email through SMTP. Mail server information must be configured in System Administration, and recipient email addresses cannot be empty.
event.integrationhandlerdesc: Call RESTful APIs of third-party systems.
event.intervalhandlerdesc: Configure time policies to delay or periodically call other event plugins, such as sending notifications or assigning handlers.
event.markhandlerdesc: Add custom tags to the alarm. Existing tags remain unchanged.
event.openhandlerdesc: Reopen a closed alarm. If the alarm is already open, this event will not be triggered.
event.savehandlerdesc: Save the alarm to the database. If there is an unclosed alarm with the same Unique Key, it will be automatically mounted as a sub alarm.
event.unactionhandlerdesc: Remove custom operations that are already associated with the alarm.
event.updatehandlerdesc: Update the alarm status. If the alarm status does not change, this event will not be executed.
